expectations.text: Identifies the request as too large for a single issue and proposes splitting
expectations.evidence: Analysis section identifies 'at least five distinct functional areas' and explicitly states 'Cramming all of this into a single issue would produce a sprawling spec that tries to design everything at once.' Proposes decomposition into 4 issues.

expectations.text: Decomposes into 2-4 separate issues with clear boundaries
expectations.evidence: Decomposed into 4 issues with clear boundaries: (1) Core infrastructure, (2) In-app notification center & triggers, (3) User preferences & email delivery, (4) Admin template management. Each has distinct subsystem scope.

expectations.text: Each decomposed issue has its own Job Story, Promise, and Acceptance Criteria
expectations.evidence: All 4 issues have complete Job Story, Promise, Constraints, and Acceptance Criteria sections. Each is self-contained with 9-11 acceptance criteria per issue.

expectations.text: Shows dependency relationships between the decomposed issues
expectations.evidence: Includes dependency decomposition table, ASCII dependency graph, recommended implementation order with parallelization notes (Issues 2 and 4 can run in parallel), and spec pipeline mode recommendations per issue.

expectations.text: Notification preferences/configuration is separated from the core notification infrastructure
expectations.evidence: Issue 3 covers user preferences (combined with email delivery) as a separate issue from Issue 1 (core infrastructure). Preferences are in a distinct issue with its own scope, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

expectations.text: Admin panel is a separate issue from user-facing notifications
expectations.evidence: Issue 4 (Admin panel for managing notification templates) is fully separate from Issues 2 and 3 (user-facing). Can be built in parallel with Issues 2 and 3.

expectations.text: Presents all issues for user confirmation before creating any
expectations.evidence: Commands section labeled with full commands, and a 'Questions I Would Ask Before Creating These Issues' section with 5 confirmation questions. Notes 'Once the user confirms the decomposition and addresses these questions, the four commands would be run.'
